notes.urn:cts:greekLit:tlg9010.tlg001.1st1K-gr: Soter (‘Saviour’) is kept as a name; it may stand for Zeus Soter. Alcomeneia and Thelxineia follow the text’s spellings.

nodes.text: 4249 ‘To look at the stars is the finest thing for men.’

4250 Astragalos [knucklebone]: properly, the thing commonly so called; also the vertebra of the neck, and the gaming-piece; and a plant too is called this. Astragalos: also the one which Belshazzar, son of Nebuchadnezzar, saw as he reclined at dinner, opposite the wall, like the knuckle of a man’s hand, writing in the Hebrew tongue things that no one could understand. Sending for Daniel, he begged him to interpret these things for him. And he said to him: ‘The knuckle that you saw is the hand of the living God; and it wrote that he has measured and completed your kingdom.’ Hearing this, Belshazzar was distressed, and a little later he was killed by Darius the Mede. Also astragalizō [I play at knucklebones].
4251 Astrampsychus, who wrote a medical book on the treatment of donkeys, and an Oneirocritica [book of dream interpretation].

4252 Astrapē [lightning]: an ignition of clouds rubbing together or burst by wind. And a proverb: ‘Lightning from a little basin’: said of worthlessness, since the flashes from springs and basins can do nothing.

2212 Praxidike: a goddess, of whom they set up only the head. Mnaseas, in his work On Europe, [says] that from Soter and his sister Praxidike were born a son, Ctesius, and daughters, Homonoia [Concord] and Arete [Virtue], who were called Praxidikai after their mother. But Dionysius in his Foundations [says that] the daughters of Ogygus, Alcomeneia, Thelxineia and Aulis, were later named Praxidikai.
